item.title: Onix CEO, Mike Nahon's Speech at Data Centre Launch in Senegal
item.dc:creator: Yinka
item.content:encoded:
On Thursday 16th of February, in Dakar, Senegal, Mike Nahon, Onix CEO, gave an in depth speech at the launch of the new Tier III neutral data centre, directly at the 2Africa cable landing station. His speech below outlines the importance of this data centre.

Ladies and gentlemen, Ambassadors, the Secretary General of the Ministry of Finance and Budget, the Secretary General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, to the representatives of the High Commander of the National, Gendarmerie, Dear partners. Ladies and gentlemen, representatives of AIIM, the General Manager of the Sonetel group. Ladies and gentlemen, representatives of the World Bank.

My thanks and gratitude conveyed to Ministers, the Government of Senegal and the people of Senegal for allowing Onix the opportunity to participate in the future of your magnificent country. You have a beautiful country with beautiful people, with enormous talent. I've enjoyed every moment that I have spent in Senegal and thank you from the bottom of my bottom of my heart for welcoming Onix into this country.

Senegal is the most stable country in Africa, growing at approximately 6% per annum. There has been a gradual slowdown because of the world circumstance; the war in the Ukraine particularly. In order to mitigate the slowdown, I think unlocking of the services economy in Senegal needs to be accessed and Onix can participate in this.

Onix own a tier IV data centred in Ghana, which promises uptime of 99.995%, which is exactly the requirement that banks, government and the hyperscalers require. We can satisfy that demand.

Before I look at the African opportunity, I think we need to understand where the facility that will be built is to be located. The facility will be located at the 2Africa cable landing station. Generally, all data that is brought to Africa is brought via an undersea cable. The undersea cable then lands at the cable landing station. From that point, another cable is laid to where the facility might be. The challenge with that is the longer the cable is, the greater the chance the cable cut or cable theft or latency. By being at the landing station, we're in an absolute prime location. The 2Africa landing cable is also the largest cable that has ever been laid; 45,000 kilometres long.

If we now look at the African paradigm, there are 4000 neutral colocation facilities in the USA, China, Germany and Great Britain. 4000!  In the African continent there are 91 neutral colocation facilities. So there are 4000 in four countries and there are 91 in Africa. In addition, Africa’s population is 17% of the world's population. So the current population is 1.3 billion and that will grow to two and a half billion by 2050. This means that one out of five people in the world will come from Africa. There is a gap between the services that we offer here and the services that are required.

The current Data centre market in Africa is $2 billion per annum. That market is expected to grow to $5 billion. In other words, increased by two and a half times by 2026. That's within four years, the market size will grow two and a half times. Approximately 700 new data facilities would be required in the short term. I think if we look at the statistics we have to conclude that there is a requirement and that Senegal is the optimal place to locate that requirement.

One of the requirements in operating a neutral facility is access to services. So any client who takes up a location in the facility must be able to access services from a number of providers, such as Sonetel for instance, such as all of the ISPs that might be present in Senegal, such as AFR-IX, who are incorporated in Spain, and offer connectivity to a number of locations worldwide.

The second thing is the environment must be rich. For instance, when you go to a shopping mall, you park your car in the basement, you go upstairs, you buy your groceries, you go to the pharmacy, you'll have a cup of coffee, and you might by a pair of shoes. The same environment needs to exist in a data centre and that is provided by the internet exchanges.

So for instance, if we look at an internet exchange like DE-CIX, they offer connectivity to 168 networks which include content providers such as Netflix, connectivity providers, as well as cloud services. We will have all of that in the facility.

You may ask what does the facility sell? The facility will sell rack space. Governments, corporates and banks will bring their servers from where they currently are into the facility and occupy rackspace. That's the first offering. The second offering is the data centre provides a location for the cloud services providers such as Microsoft Azure, Google and AWS.

What is happening means cloud services are being accessed by the local markets in places such as Ireland. That brings two results. Number one, we're in breach of the data sovereignty rules and number two, all the revenue that is paid for those services is lost to countries offshore. By creating this facility we will have access to cloud services in country, securing services onshore, trapping the revenue onshore to a major boost to the economy.

In addition, one would ask, “banks will occupy the facility, government will occupy the facility. But what about the hyperscaler?” The hyperscalers such as Facebook or Netflix or Google or any of the hyperscalers coming and taking up residence onshore means that a greater percentage of revenue will be hard currency which also benefit to the economy. The other opportunities are that more job opportunities are created, plus the local workforce is upskilled. If we look at the fact there are 4000 data centres in four countries alone, with very few data centres, particularly in West Africa, one has to conclude that the time is opportune for us to build these data centres here.

One then has to say Senegal is the optimum location to build data centres. Why? Because it's a stable environment and there's a stable currency as the CFA is linked to the Euro. There is an inherent lack of sovereign risk in this country.

The next point to consider is the location of the facility. It's located at the cable landing station. There are very few data centre facilities that are built at the landing station and that for us is a big, big plus. So the combination of the landing station in Senegal, the currency, the people, and the skillsets, mitigate for this development in Senegal. If I can give you an analogy, if one had to look at Singapore, for example, Singapore has a small land mass, it has a small population, but has a disproportionate number of data sensors. And I think Senegal will be the next Singapore.

By creating these neutral colocation facilities in Senegal, in this environment, we will attract all of the hyperscalers and encourage them to locate within senegal and we can satisfy their needs without doubt.

I think that speech in English is probably coming to an end, but I have to say a great thank you to Sonetel and Mrs Dieng. She's put up with me and my English language now for 18 months or so. And I'm very appreciative of the relationship that we have developed and all the support that you've given me.

I have to thank my Senegalese family, which is CCDOC La Colombe, led by joint Managing Directors Mr. Djiby and Pape Gueye.

I have to thank Mr Mamadu Kebe, the Senegalese Managing Director of Onix. I have to thank the Chief of Development in the region, Miss Awa Fall, and I have to thank you again for your patience, your guidance, and for steering me in the direction and allowing us to implement what we have got here today.

I then must not forget AIIM, the majority shareholder in Onix for their support in difficult times because the world economy has not been great, and for their support for allowing us to access the future. Lastly, I have to thank my expanded Onix Team. Without you, there's no possibility that we would have got to, when we have it today. So thank you all. Thank you for your time.

item.title: Colocation Data Centres: Maximising Security, Connectivity, Capital
item.dc:creator: Yinka
item.content:encoded:
A colocation data centre is a type of data centre facility that allows businesses to rent space for their servers and other computing hardware. These data centres typically provide a secure and controlled environment for businesses to house their hardware, as well as the necessary power, cooling, and networking infrastructure to keep the hardware running smoothly. 

Outsourcing Hardware Management

Colocation data centres, like those of Onix in Accra and Senegal, offer a number of benefits for businesses. One of the main advantages is that they allow businesses to outsource the management and maintenance of their hardware to a third party. This can be especially useful for small and medium-sized businesses that may not have the resources or expertise to manage their own data centre infrastructure. 

Enhanced Security Measures

Another benefit of colocation data centres is that they provide a high level of security for businesses' hardware. These data centres are typically equipped with advanced security measures such as biometric scanners, security cameras, and perimeter fencing to prevent unauthorised access. In addition, they often have redundant power, cooling systems and fire suppression technology in place to ensure that the hardware remains operational in the event of a power outage or other unforeseen event. In the case of Onix Tier IV data centre in Accra, it also has a 2200 panel solar farm, providing day time off grid electricity. This means no reliance on grid power during the day and savings for customers, as well as sustainable operations.

Connectivity Options

Colocation data centres are also designed to provide businesses with a high level of connectivity. These data centres typically offer a range of networking options, including dedicated fibre optic connections and multiple internet service providers (ISPs). This allows businesses to connect to the internet and other networks with a high level of reliability and performance. 

Location Considerations

One of the main considerations for businesses when choosing a colocation data centre is location. Data centres are typically located in areas with a reliable power grid and good connectivity to major internet exchanges. Some businesses may also choose a data centre based on its proximity to their own offices or other key locations. In the case of Onix, it is located outside of any earthquake and industry zones to ensure the safety of data at all times.

Cost Savings with Colocation Data Centres

In addition to the physical infrastructure and location, businesses also need to consider the level of support and services offered by the colocation data centre. Many data centres offer a range of services such as remote hands support, where technicians are available to assist with hardware installation or maintenance tasks, and managed services, where the data centre manages the hardware on behalf of the business. 

Overall, a colocation data centre is a valuable resource for businesses that need a secure and reliable place to house their hardware and connect to the internet and other networks. These data centres offer a range of benefits, including the ability to outsource hardware management, high levels of security and connectivity, and a range of support and service options.

item.title: Senegal, the Next Singapore: Why Now is the Time to Invest
item.dc:creator: Yinka
item.content:encoded:
Senegal, located at the most western point of the African continent in the Atlantic Ocean and at the crossroads of major sea and air routes is quickly becoming a hot spot for investors looking for new opportunity.  

Digital Transformation in Senegal

Senegal's digital transformation journey is set to receive another boost with the announcement that Onix Data Centre will be launching a new facility at the 2Africa cable landing station in Dakar. With its top-ranking connectivity and ongoing efforts to foster a thriving digital economy, Senegal is well on its way to becoming a key player in Africa's rapidly evolving technology landscape. This latest development is expected to further enhance the country's reputation as a leading digital hub in the region. 

Senegal's Growing Economy 

One of the main reasons Senegal is so attractive to investors is its rapidly growing economy. In the last decade, Senegal has seen a steady increase in GDP, with a growth rate of around 6% in 2019. This is largely due to the government's focus on developing its infrastructure and promoting foreign investment. The construction of new highways, airports, and ports has made it easier for businesses to operate in the country, while tax incentives and other policies have made it more attractive for foreign companies to invest in Senegal. 

Political Stability in Senegal 

Another major factor that makes Senegal a great place to invest is its stable political environment. The country has a long tradition of peaceful transitions of power and a strong commitment to democracy. This has helped to create a sense of security for investors, who know that their investments will be protected regardless of who is in power. 

Senegal's Large and Growing Consumer Market 

In addition to its strong economy and stable political environment, Senegal also has a large and growing consumer market. With a population of over 17 million people and a rapidly growing middle class, Senegal offers a huge potential market for companies selling consumer goods and services. This is particularly true in sectors such as retail, tourism, and real estate, which are all expected to experience significant growth in the coming years. 

Skilled Workforce in Senegal 

Finally, Senegal has a well-educated and hardworking workforce, making it an attractive destination for companies looking to set up operations in Africa. The country has a high literacy rate and a large number of people with technical skills, making it an ideal location for businesses looking to tap into Africa's growing market for goods and services. 

Conclusion - Senegal: The Next Singapore 

In conclusion, Senegal is a country on the rise and it's poised to become the next Singapore in terms of investment potential. With a rapidly growing economy, fast moving digital transformation, a stable political environment, a large and growing consumer market, and a well-educated workforce - make Senegal an ideal place to invest. And with the world economy still recovering from the COVID-19 pandemic, now is the perfect time for businesses to take advantage of the opportunities that Senegal has to offer, which is exactly why Onix data centres have taken the exciting step of launching a facility in Dakar.

item.title: Cold Aisle Containment: The Key to Efficient Data Centre Cooling in Tropical Climates
item.dc:creator: Yinka
item.content:encoded:
Data Centres have become a vital part of our worldwide infrastructure, but they are vulnerable technological organisms creating their own weaknesses. One of the weaknesses is brought about by the large rate of electricity consumption needed to run a data centre 24/7. That electricity leads to exceptionally hot environments and due to their nature, data centres can not simply be shut down to rest and cool down. If not mitigated against, performance can be greatly reduced and with frequent failures and increased downtime.  

Dealing with heat in a data centre can be even more challenging in tropical countries. To maintain a Tier IV status, a data centre, it is imperative that a facility has a world class cooling system.  

In a colocation data centre, such as that of Onix in Accra, Ghana, as more and more servers are added to the racks, the temperature increases. As the temperature rises, servers will stop performing at their peak levels and are susceptible to burning out entirely. There are various methods used to cool large colocation data centres, such as water-cooled chiller plant, air cooled chiller plant and direct evaporating cooling. In this article we will discuss the direct expansion, cold aisle system used by Onix in Accra.  

The facility in Accra, a city with an average daily temperature of 30°C (86°F), currently houses 170 racks in its initial data room. It uses a technique called Cold Aisle Containment (CAC) as its main defence against the immense heat caused by this number of servers in a tropical climate.  

With CAC the cold aisle is enclosed between the server racks, which face each other, with doors at either end of the aisle. The floor tiles running down the aisle, in front of both racks, are perforated.  Cold air is blown through these tiles and contained within the aisle, and therefore delivered directly to the server equipment air intakes. The containment aisle means that the cold air does not mix with warm air and reaches the servers without obstruction. This is termed ‘focus cooling. 

The question now is, where does all the warm air from the servers go? Well, the heated air from the servers is forced out of the back and then recycled into the Computer Room Air conditioning (CRAC) unit. From here it is cooled and passes back into the system to cool the room and the CAC. 

The direct expansion CRAC units work in a similar manner to those you may have in your homes or have experienced in hotels. The difference is these devices can function continuously for a year without a pause. The cooling function is provided by blowing cool air over a cooling coil, filled with a refrigerant, which is kept cool by a compressor within the unit. 

This then completes the cycle by pumping the air through the raised floor and through the perforated tiles into the CAC. The system also monitors the temperature, air distribution and humidity in the data centre to maintain a balanced climate throughout the day. With the raised floor, which was built into the architecture, and the CAC, cooling can be made for 30kW heat load per rack.  Each CRAC in our Data Hall has a heat energy of 104kW. 

Want to see our direct expansion cold aisle containment technology in action? Take a video tour of our data centre's Tier IV cooling system, where we use this cutting-edge technique to keep our servers cool and operating at peak efficiency in the hot and humid climate of Accra, Ghana. Watch the video below to see how our innovative cooling system works, and how we maintain a 99.995% uptime for our clients. Contact us if you want any further information.

item.title: Securing Your Data: Advanced Fire Suppression in Data Centres
item.dc:creator: Yinka
item.content:encoded:
Despite the minimal risk of fire at a data centre, it's crucial to protect against fire damage. A fire can be potentially devastating for a data centre and its clients. In this blog, we'll discuss the design features and high-tech systems used at data centres, like Onix Data Centre in Accra, to mitigate fire risks.

Video Announcement

For a closer look at the fire suppression systems in action at Onix Data Centre in Accra, we've prepared a video tour, shot within the data centre itself. This exclusive footage provides an in-depth understanding of how these advanced systems operate to ensure the safety and security of your data. To watch the video, simply click on the embedded player below.

Architectural Design Features for Fire Mitigation

The planning for fire mitigation at data centres, such as Onix Data Centre in Accra, starts at the design phase. Materials like concrete walls and fire-rated FD120 doors are carefully chosen for their fire-resisting capacity. Data halls have spacing of 1.5 metres around them to mitigate against external fire risks.

Early Warning Fire Detection Systems

State-of-the-art fire detection systems like VESDA (Very Early Smoke Detection Apparatus) play a vital role in alerting the team of a fire at the earliest stage. The air sampling fire detection system at Onix Data Centre in Accra can detect invisible by-products of materials as they degrade during pre-combustion stages of a fire.

Automated Fire Suppression Systems

In addition to fire extinguishers, data centres like Onix in Accra need automated systems for quick fire suppression. Systems like the Kidde Fire Systems Natura™ Inert Gas System release a mixture of argon and nitrogen upon detection of a fire, extinguishing it without damaging technology or posing a threat to humans.

Conclusion

Advanced fire detection and suppression systems, such as those employed by Onix Data Centre in Accra, are essential for maintaining data centre reliability and uptime. By implementing these measures, data centres can ensure uninterrupted service and the highest level of security for their clients' data.

item.title: Protecting Your Data: The Importance of Data Security for Businesses and Institutions
item.dc:creator: Yinka
item.content:encoded:
Why Data Security Matters for Businesses and Institutions

When you entrust your data to a business or institution, you want to be sure that it is safe and secure. After all, your sensitive personal or financial information could be at risk in the event of a data breach or other cyber threat. That's why it's important to choose businesses and institutions that take data security seriously and partner with data centres that have the highest level of certification and stringent security measures.

How Data Centres Support Businesses and Institutions in Protecting Data

Data centres play a critical role in supporting businesses and institutions in protecting their data. By providing a secure, controlled environment with state-of-the-art security measures and backup solutions, data centres can help mitigate the risk of data loss, theft, or damage caused by physical or digital threats. In addition, data centres offer businesses and institutions the ability to scale their infrastructure quickly and efficiently, without the need to invest in costly on-premises equipment and facilities. This enables organisations to focus on their core operations while relying on the expertise of the data centre provider to manage their critical data and infrastructure.

Why It's Crucial to Choose Businesses with Stringent Data Security Measures?

In today's world, data breaches and cyber threats are becoming more common and sophisticated, and businesses of all sizes are at risk. When you entrust your personal or financial information to a business or institution, it's critical to ensure that they have adequate measures in place to protect it. By choosing companies that take data security seriously, you can rest assured that your data is being managed effectively and in compliance with regulatory requirements. Data breaches can lead to a loss of customer trust, damage to reputation, financial losses, and even legal liabilities. It's essential to partner with businesses and institutions that prioritise data protection and have strict security measures in place to mitigate these risks. Choosing a business or institution that values data protection can give you peace of mind and protect your personal and financial information.

A cold containment aisle in Onix Data Centre, Accra
The Importance of Comprehensive Backup and Redundancy Solutions

Choosing a data centre with a comprehensive backup and redundancy solution can ensure that your data is always available, even in the event of a disaster or other unforeseen event. At Onix Data Centre, we offer our clients redundant power and cooling systems, network connectivity, and storage solutions, ensuring that their data is always available and protected.

The Role of Certification and Security Measures

When it comes to sensitive data such as banking records or medical records, it's especially important to choose businesses and institutions that partner with data centres with the highest level of certification and security measures. By doing so, you can rest assured that your data is being managed effectively and in compliance with regulatory requirements. In today's world, data breaches and cyber threats are becoming more common, and businesses of all sizes are at risk. This is why it's important to choose a data centre with the highest level of certification, such as ISO 27001, which demonstrates that they have rigorous security measures in place to protect your data.

Choosing Onix Data Centre

By choosing businesses and institutions that partner with data centres like Onix Data Centre, you can have peace of mind knowing that your data is protected and always available when you need it. At Onix Data Centre, we are committed to providing businesses and institutions with the highest level of data security and backup solutions.

If you would like any other information on this topic please get in contact.

item.title: Onix Data Centres Launches New Neutral Colocation Data Centre in Senegal
item.dc:creator: Samuel
item.content:encoded:
Enhancing Connectivity and Driving Economic Advancement in West Africa

On 16th of February, 2023, Onix Data Centres Ltd announced the launch of its second West African neutral colocation data centre. Expanding on its existing Tier IV data centre in Ghana, the new data centre is strategically located in Dakar, Senegal, at the 2Africa Cable Landing Station (“CLS”). The 2Africa cable is 45,000km long and connects Africa, Europe, and Asia

The fully integrated neutral colocation facility gives customers the ability to connect to all submarine cables in Senegal (ACE, MainOne, 2Africa) in a wholesale environment, resulting in unprecedented low latency global connectivity. This is of great benefit to financial institutions and enterprises who require mission critical access to global cloud providers.  Onix leverages SDN-ready partners to ease migration and onboarding to its data centres. 

Centrally located, Senegal offers low sovereign risk with strong institutions and an educated workforce. The country is undergoing significant economic advancement led by the exploitation of the oil and gas shelf by BP, which will soon rank Senegal as the 4th biggest producer of gas worldwide. Applications and data hosted in Senegal will be accessible across the African continent over multiple submarine cables at lower latencies which clearly provides significant advantages over hosting in Europe or North America.

The exploitation of the oil and gas shelf is likely to lead to further significant foreign direct investment into the country. Senegal will feature very significantly in the development of data centres in West Africa, facilitating the hosting of corporates, as well as providers of cloud service solutions.

“The launch on 16 February 2023 of the data centre in Senegal is an exciting step forward in our mission to provide superior neutral colocation services and connectivity to our customers in West Africa,” said Michael Nahon, Onix CEO.

La Colombe Group joint CEO, Pape Gueye, Onix’s partner in Senegal, stated “the launch of the first neutral Data Centre at the CLS in Senegal, and on the African continent, will bring significant benefits not only to local businesses, but also to governments and public institutions in the region. By providing secure and reliable access to data services, the data centre can support the digitisation efforts of these organisations, helping them to improve their services and better serve their communities. Additionally, the data sovereignty aspect of the centre ensures that sensitive information is protected and remains within the jurisdiction of the country and the West African Zone, which is of utmost importance in today's data-driven world.”

With two data centres in Africa, Ghana’s only Tier IV Data centre and the newly launched facility in Senegal, Onix is uniquely positioned to offer unparalleled service to customers seeking a central hub for West Africa.

For Media Interest please contact: - Samuel@onixdc.wpcomstaging.com

item.title: Ensuring 99.995% Uptime: Power Backup Systems at Onix Data Centre in Accra, Ghana
item.dc:creator: Yinka
item.content:encoded:
The Importance of Reliable Data Centres 

Data Centres are crucial for businesses around the world, offering reliable, continuous service to ensure that data is always accessible. Any period of downtime can significantly affect a business's operations. To ensure that data access is uninterrupted, it's crucial for data centres to have robust backup power systems. 

Onix Data Centre: Guaranteeing 99.995% Uptime 

Onix Data Centre, a leading provider of data centre services in Accra, Ghana, is committed to ensuring 99.995% uptime - a requirement for our Tier IV certification. We utilise a combination of generators, Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS), grid and solar energy systems to ensure continuous service. This reliable power supply is not only vital for data access but also ensures that cooling, climate control systems, fire suppression systems, and security systems operate without interruption. 

Watch our video below to see how we maintain 99.995% uptime at Onix Data Centre 
Our Power Backup Systems: Generators and UPS 

Located outside the data centre facility, we have three independent SDMO Kohler generator sets. Each of these generators can deliver 446 kVa of power in the event of a power outage, a common occurrence in emerging economies like Ghana. These generators, colour-coded for easy identification, can restore power to the facility within 12 seconds of a grid and solar power disconnect. During this brief period, our UPS systems sustain power until the transfer to an alternative power source is complete. 

Our power system also includes two sets of Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) units, which provide emergency power when the primary power source fails. The 300kVA Eaton UPS supports IT load for up to 25 minutes, while the 150kVA Eaton cooling UPS can provide 12 minutes of power, with the facility operating at full capacity. Once grid or solar power is restored, the UPS units are recharged. 

Guaranteed Power, Uninterrupted Service 

Despite the robustness of our solar energy, grid energy, and backup generators, we have UPS systems in place to ensure that there is time to rectify any issues and restore power without any noticeable impact on the client. 

Why Choose Onix Data Centre? 

Many companies opt for colocation data centres like Onix because their own head offices cannot guarantee a reliable power source for their servers. This is particularly true for businesses operating in markets with unreliable power sources. Besides reducing costs of housing and maintaining an in-house data centre, companies using colocation data centres are assured that their data will always be securely stored and continuously accessible. 

Get in Touch 

To learn more about our reliable data centre services and how we can help your business maintain continuous data access, contact us today. At Onix Data Centre, we're committed to providing the best data centre services in Accra, Ghana.

item.title: Solar-Powered Data Storage: Onix's Sustainable Solution
item.dc:creator: Samuel
item.content:encoded:
Data centres play a crucial role in our digital age. To operate effectively, they require a steady, reliable power source. This is particularly true in the developing world, where grid power can be scarce. Innovative technology can bridge this gap, as demonstrated by the Onix Data Centre in Accra, Ghana. At Onix, we utilise three 446kVA continuous rated capacity backup generators, as well as our own solar farm, adjacent to the facility.

Global Data Usage and the Importance of Sustainability

As data usage grows exponentially around the world – projected to reach 220 zettabytes (ZB) in 2023, up from 33 ZB in 2018 – the energy demand of data centres increases accordingly. Recognising this, we have prioritised sustainability from the outset.

Harnessing the Power of the Sun at Onix

Though Onix has backup generators for emergencies, we rely heavily on our solar farm. This facility consists of 2200 panels, each with a power output of 330W, for a total potential output of 726,000 Wp. However, due to the inherent inefficiencies in solar power, the peak power is 640kW, enough to power approximately 213 average UK homes each day.

Virtual Tour of Our Solar Farm

Below, you can take a virtual tour of our state-of-the-art solar farm and see how we harness the power of the sun to support our data centre's operations:

Planning for Future Expansion

Our solar farm's potential output is significantly higher than the current needs of our data centre. This was intentionally planned to allow for increased capacity at Onix. We can cover additional power needs by simply increasing the current output from the solar farm - a process that can be managed remotely with minimal effort.

Regular maintenance of a solar farm is imperative to keep it running reliably and at maximum potential efficiency. This means that the panels must be cleaned regularly, especially in dusty climates such as that in Accra, Ghana. In the case of the data centre at Onix, it takes about 8 days for the maintenance crew to clean the entire 2200 panels, checking for any other issues as they do so.

Once produced, the solar power is transported through inverters directly to our facility's power room. Here, an automatic system determines which energy source – solar or national grid – should be used. The power then feeds into our server room, where each rack is served by two power sources to ensure there is no interruption in power. This is vital to provide a reliable service to clients.

Onix's Commitment to Environmental Sustainability

In a time when Africa faces the highest risk from the impending climate crisis, Onix is committed to reducing our environmental impact. One way we achieve this is by feeding any excess power back into the national grid during the day. While we await necessary permissions from the Electricity Company Ghana, we are exploring other solutions like powerful battery systems to utilise solar power 24/7.

At Onix, we are proud to have built renewable energy into our data storage plans from the very beginning. We continually optimise our data usage and stay updated with industry trends to bring further efficiencies that benefit both the environment and our customers.

The solar plant generates about 1200kWh of energy per day. Although our solar plant's capacity is 640kW, to prevent excessive export onto the national grid due to the limited load on our data centre, we have reduced the maximum plant output to 105kW.

Connect with Onix

For further information about our power system, contingencies, or how our colocation facilities can meet your data storage needs, please contact us at info@onixdatacentres.com

item.title: The Role of Data Centres in Smart Cities: The Future of Urban Living in Africa
item.dc:creator: Samuel
item.content:encoded:
Smart cities are swiftly becoming a buzzword across the globe, but in Africa, they present a unique promise and set of challenges. At the heart of these burgeoning urban landscapes is the silent workhorse: the data centre. Onix Data Centres, with operations spanning across the continent, stands at the forefront of this transformative journey.

Africa's Urbanisation: A Unique Landscape

As Africa witnesses rapid urban growth, its cities grapple with myriad issues, from infrastructural deficits to energy access. Smart cities, with their efficiency and interconnectedness, offer an innovative solution, tailoring global technological advancements to Africa's distinct landscape.

The Data-Driven Backbone: African Data Centres

Emerging as the nexus of this transformation, data centres like Onix Data Centres ensure that Africa's smart cities are anchored in reliable, localised data processing and storage. By offering immediate and culturally-relevant data solutions, these centres become pivotal in enhancing urban responsiveness, whilst prioritising data security and sovereignty.

Key Areas of Integration in African Cities

Transportation: As major African cities tackle congestion, intelligent traffic systems provide respite. The potential of adapting autonomous vehicles to African terrains becomes an exciting avenue for exploration.

Energy Management: Smart grids offer consistency in regions battling with power outages, seamlessly integrating Africa's abundant renewable energy sources.

Public Safety: Data centres play a crucial role in processing vast amounts of information from surveillance systems, ensuring urban safety. Moreover, their capabilities prove invaluable during natural disasters, directing swift emergency responses.

Healthcare: Telemedicine bridges the urban-rural divide, with data centres ensuring that patient data is secure, centralised, and readily accessible.

Infrastructure Maintenance: In a continent with diverse infrastructural challenges, IoT sensors, powered by reliable data centres, monitor and maintain crucial utilities, from roads to water supply systems.

Sustainability: An African Perspective

Beyond service efficiency, data centres in Africa, like Onix Data Centres, are shaping sustainability narratives. As they support smart city initiatives tackling desertification, water scarcity, and more, they also evolve to adopt green designs and practices, cognisant of Africa's unique climatic considerations.

Challenges and Afrocentric Considerations

Africa's rich tapestry of cultures, languages, and traditions necessitates a unique approach to data-driven solutions. Ensuring inclusivity and relevance while navigating this diverse landscape is paramount. Onix Data Centres, with its deep-rooted presence in Africa, remains attuned to these nuances, moulding its solutions accordingly.

Smart cities in Africa are not mere replications of a global trend; they're a testament to the continent's adaptability and innovation. Onix Data Centres, in its pivotal role, champions this vision, driving Africa towards a future where urban living is efficient, sustainable, and uniquely African.

Witness firsthand the transformative power of state-of-the-art data centres in shaping Africa's urban future. Discover more about Onix Data Centres and their role in this exciting journey.

item.title: Strategic Network Peering: A Beginners Guide
item.dc:creator: Samuel
item.content:encoded:
This August, the Onix team had the privilege of attending AfPIF in Accra, where we met a diverse group of experts from across the peering world. One of the standout presentations was by Euro IX, who introduced their comprehensive Peering Toolbox. This invaluable resource has informed much of what we discuss here, as we delve into the strategic value and complexities of network peering. The question we aim to answer is: are organisations truly capitalising on the multifaceted benefits of network peering?

What is Network Peering?

Network peering is the practice of interconnecting separate Internet networks for the purpose of exchanging traffic directly, rather than through a third party. This direct connection results in reduced latency, lower costs, and improved speed and reliability of data transfer. Peering can be either public, facilitated through an Internet Exchange Point (IXP), or private, occurring directly between two networks. It's a practice that has evolved from simple, bilateral agreements to complex, multi-lateral relationships involving various stakeholders like ISPs, CDNs, and IXPs.

The Strategic Value of Peering

In today's competitive landscape, particularly for sectors like finance, healthcare, and e-commerce, the strategic implications of advanced peering strategies are immense. These can translate into tangible business benefits such as improved network performance, reduced operational costs, and enhanced user experience. Advanced peering also allows for better control over network resources, enabling organisations to prioritise critical services and manage bandwidth more effectively. But the question arises: is your organisation equipped to navigate the complexities and challenges that come with advanced peering?

Advanced Peering Strategies
  • Selective Peering: The focus here is on quality over quantity. Networks should aim for peering relationships that offer the most value in terms of latency, throughput, and reliability. This involves a careful analysis of traffic patterns, performance metrics, and business objectives.
  • Traffic Engineering: Advanced peering strategies often employ Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) attributes to influence the path that network traffic takes. This allows for more efficient routing, optimised performance, and better control over the network's traffic flow.
  • Multi-Homing: This involves connecting to multiple ISPs for redundancy and performance benefits. Multi-homing is a step up from basic peering and offers an additional layer of reliability. As network management strategies continue to evolve, have you considered incorporating advanced techniques like multi-homing?
Considerations for Businesses
  • Cost-Efficiency: One of the most immediate benefits of direct peering is the significant cost savings it offers. Through our peering partners, Onix Data Centre can facilitate these savings for your business.
  • Performance: The direct nature of peering allows for quicker data transfers, crucial for businesses that rely on real-time data analytics. Onix Data Centre, in collaboration with our peering partners, prioritises performance to meet your business needs.
  • Data Control: Direct connections offer more control over how data is routed. Trust Onix Data Centre and our peering partners to provide secure and efficient routing solutions for your sensitive or regulated information.
Security in Advanced Peering

In the context of increasing cybersecurity threats, implementing robust security measures like BGP Route Validation and Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI) is non-negotiable for securing advanced peering relationships.

Conclusion

Network peering is not just a technical configuration but a strategic initiative with far-reaching implications on operational efficiency and business performance. For those looking for a comprehensive guide on this subject, the Peering Toolbox by Euro-IX is highly recommended.

Take the Next Step with Onix Data Centre

Ready to implement advanced peering strategies in your organisation? Onix Data Centre, in partnership with our trusted peering partners, can facilitate this transition. Contact us today for a consultation and discover how we can help you optimise your network for success.

item.title: Resilience in Data Centres: Preparing for Natural Disasters
item.dc:creator: Samuel
item.content:encoded:
Natural disasters like floods, earthquakes, and hurricanes pose significant threats to the integrity and continuity of data centre operations. Ensuring that your data centre can withstand these challenges is crucial for maintaining uninterrupted service. This blog post delves into the key considerations for preparing data centres for natural disasters, with a special focus on Onix Data Centre's best practices in Accra, Ghana.

Understanding the Risks in Data Centre Operations

Natural disasters can cause catastrophic damage to data centres. Whether you're dealing with flooding in low-lying areas, seismic activity in earthquake-prone regions, or storms in coastal locations, understanding the regional risks is essential. Real-world examples underscore the need for robust data centre resilience planning, tailored to the specific risks of each location.

Building a Resilient Data Centre Infrastructure

The cornerstone of a resilient data centre is its meticulously planned design and construction. Site selection takes into account geographical and climatic factors to minimise the risks posed by natural disasters. Structural considerations involve utilising materials and designs that can withstand extreme conditions. Power supply resilience is achieved through redundant power sources and uninterruptible power systems (UPS) to ensure continuous operation. Cooling systems are designed to function effectively in a variety of weather conditions.

Implementing Robust Data Centre Disaster Recovery Plans

An effective disaster recovery plan serves as the backbone of a resilient data centre. It goes beyond mere data backup; it's a comprehensive strategy that ensures business continuity in the face of unforeseen challenges. Regularly backing up data to multiple locations is a fundamental step, but it's equally important to have failover procedures in place. These procedures allow for automatic system transfer in the event of a failure, minimising downtime. Emergency response protocols establish clear procedures for reacting to natural disasters, from immediate actions to long-term recovery plans. Routine tests are conducted to ensure that these recovery plans are not only effective but also up-to-date with the latest threats and technologies.

Technological Solutions for Data Centre Resilience

Technology plays a pivotal role in enhancing data centre resilience. Advanced sensors and monitoring systems provide early warnings of potential disasters, allowing for proactive measures to be taken. Cloud infrastructure offers redundancy and rapid recovery options, serving as a secondary line of defence against data loss. Virtualisation technologies enable efficient backup and restoration processes, allowing for quicker recovery times and less operational disruption. These technological solutions are integrated into the data centre's overall resilience strategy, ensuring a multi-layered approach to disaster preparedness.

Regulatory Compliance and Data Centre Standards in Accra

Adherence to legal requirements and industry standards is not just a formality; it's paramount for maintaining the reputation and integrity of data centre operations in Accra and beyond. Compliance ensures that the data centre meets or exceeds guidelines set by governmental bodies and industry organisations. This involves regular audits, certifications, and updates to meet evolving regulations. Non-compliance can result in hefty fines and a tarnished reputation, making it crucial for data centres to stay abreast of the latest legal requirements and industry best practices.

Onix Data Centre's Comprehensive Approach to Resilience in Accra
  • Site Selection
  • Structural Design
  • Power Supply Resilience
  • Cooling Systems
  • Disaster Recovery Plans
  • Monitoring and Detection Systems
  • Compliance and Standards
  • Real-life Scenarios or Case Studies
The Importance of Data Centre Resilience in Accra

Data centre resilience is not merely a technical challenge; it's a comprehensive strategy involving careful planning, robust infrastructure, and continuous adaptation. Onix Data Centre's approach exemplifies the commitment to providing resilient data centre solutions in Accra, prepared to withstand the unforeseen challenges of natural disasters.

Secure Your Data with Onix Data Centre in Accra

Interested in learning more about resilient data centre solutions at Onix Data Centre in Accra? Contact us today to explore how we can support your business in navigating the complexities of disaster preparedness.

item.title: Revolutionising Healthcare Through Colocation Data Centre Solutions
item.dc:creator: Samuel
item.content:encoded:
The Digital Transformation in Healthcare via Colocation

In today's digital age, healthcare is increasingly dependent on data centres. Colocation data centres, where multiple organisations rent space for servers and hardware, have become particularly vital. This blog explores the unique advantages and challenges of using colocation data centres in healthcare.

The Centrality of Colocation Data Centres in Healthcare

Colocation data centres have become the cornerstone of modern healthcare. By offering a shared environment, they provide healthcare organisations with cost-effective, scalable, and secure solutions for data storage and management. Their role is not just to house data but to facilitate real-time analytics, telemedicine, and secure data exchange, thereby directly affecting patient outcomes and operational efficiency.

DC Power Maintenance: Sustainable and Reliable Solutions at Onix Data Centre

In the unique environment of a colocation data centre, the significance of DC power maintenance cannot be overstated. At Onix Data Centre, we take this a step further by incorporating sustainable energy solutions. Our state-of-the-art solar farm not only reduces our carbon footprint but also ensures a consistent and reliable power supply to all our tenants. In addition to solar energy, we have robust backup generators that kick in automatically in the event of any power failure. This dual approach guarantees uninterrupted power, minimising the risk of downtime and data loss—factors that are especially critical in healthcare settings.

Real-time Monitoring: The Necessity in Colocation Data Centres

Real-time monitoring in a colocation data centre is not just a feature; it's a necessity. Given the shared nature of resources, healthcare organisations must have real-time insights into the performance and health of their colocated infrastructure. Advanced monitoring systems offer predictive analytics, alerting tenants to potential issues such as overheating or system failures before they escalate, thereby ensuring the integrity of healthcare data systems.

Uninterruptible Power Supplies: The Colocation Safety Net

In a colocation environment, uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) serve as the ultimate safety net. They ensure that healthcare systems remain operational, even during power outages, by providing a reliable backup power source. Given that multiple healthcare organisations may rely on the same colocation centre, a robust UPS system is essential for ensuring uninterrupted patient care.

The Future of Healthcare Lies in Colocation

As healthcare continues to evolve, colocation data centres will play an increasingly significant role. By focusing on robust DC power maintenance, real-time monitoring, and uninterruptible power supplies, healthcare organisations can leverage the benefits of colocation to deliver high-quality patient care.

In today's rapidly evolving healthcare landscape, choosing the right colocation data centre can make all the difference. Onix Data Centre offers state-of-the-art facilities, robust DC power maintenance, real-time monitoring, and uninterruptible power supplies to meet the unique demands of healthcare organisations. Don't compromise on your healthcare data management. Choose reliability, choose security, choose Onix Data Centre.

Contact us today to schedule a consultation and take the first step towards optimising your healthcare data management.

item.title: Community Solidarity: Onix Data Centre's Support for South Tongu Flood Relief
item.dc:creator: Samuel
item.content:encoded:
The southern Volta region has been struck by a severe flood, a dire consequence of dam spillage compounded by relentless rains. The communities in South Tongu are grappling with unprecedented devastation—homes submerged, vital resources lost, and the rhythm of daily life shattered. As we unfold the narrative of this disaster and Onix Data Centre's immediate response, we invite you to join us at the forefront of these relief efforts. Read on to discover the impact of the calamity and how your support can provide a lifeline to those in dire need.

Onix Data Centre's Response

In response to the urgent needs arising from the flood disaster, Onix Data Centres, an Accra-based data centre, collaborated with the Agave Development Association to provide practical aid to the stricken communities. Samuel Polley, who has a longstanding bond with South Tongu, coordinated the outreach, ensuring that the aid was both meaningful and timely. The Onix team, including Serwaa Kankam and Michael Thompson, made the journey from Accra to Sogakope, bringing with them essential supplies to aid in relief efforts.

The team delivered substantial quantities of local rice and yellow maize, along with numerous bags of pure water, to address the immediate needs for food and clean drinking water. These staples were chosen for their fundamental role in sustaining the affected communities during the recovery period.

The Onix Team in Action

The team was warmly received by local leaders and community members, who were essential to the day's relief efforts. Despite Yao Amekor's absence due to illness, his preparatory work was crucial to the operation's success. The team's visit to the District Chief Executive's office was a prelude to a day dedicated to providing tangible support to those in need.

Reaching the Forgotten

The outreach focused on Dekporta, Ziwoenu, and Amuto—communities that had received little attention in the wake of the flooding. The Onix team was confronted with the stark reality of the disaster's impact, witnessing the extensive damage and hearing the courageous stories of local fishermen who risked their lives to save others. The distribution of the rice, maize, and water was met with heartfelt cheers, highlighting the importance of such relief efforts. The community's reaction to the arrival of these supplies was a powerful testament to the value of the relief efforts.

A Message of Hope and Safety

Community members expressed their gratitude to the Onix and ADA teams, emphasising the need for continued support. ADA executive Evelyn Goni cautioned the communities about health risks, while Samuel Polley shared a message of unity and resilience, encouraging the communities to remain steadfast in their journey towards recovery.

Onix Data Centre's involvement in the South Tongu relief effort is a reflection of our commitment to community support and collective action. We are part of a larger community effort to assist those in need, and our contribution is just one aspect of the broader support network.

You Can Support

Onix Data Centre is dedicated to supporting the South Tongu community, and we encourage others to join us in this effort. If you or your organisation wish to contribute to the flood relief initiatives, we are here to facilitate your involvement. Contact Samuel Polley and our team for guidance on how to provide effective aid. Together, we can ensure that our combined efforts bring relief and hope to those affected by the floods.
item.excerpt:encoded: In the wake of South Tongu's devastating floods, Onix Data Centre, alongside the Agave Development Association and other contributors, mobilized a significant relief operation. Delivering essential food supplies and clean water, we witnessed the community's resilience firsthand. Each sack of rice, maize, and water symbolized our collective commitment to aid and rebuild. This united effort, a testament to the power of collaboration, has sparked a beacon of hope amidst the adversity. We extend our heartfelt thanks to all who have joined in these crucial support initiatives.

item.title: Onix Data Centre: Aligning with Africa's Data Centre and Cloud Services Revolution

In the wake of the transformative growth within Sub-Saharan Africa's data centre and cloud services landscape, as detailed in the "Africa Interconnection Report 2023", Onix Data Centre stands at the forefront of this revolution. The report highlights an unprecedented investment in carrier-neutral data centres across the continent, with an estimated US$5-6 billion expected to be infused in the next 3-5 years. This expansion is not just confined to traditional tech hubs but is increasingly permeating countries like Ghana. The Africa Interconnection Report 2023 has been put together brilliantly by Balancing Act and our good friends over at Console Connect.

At Onix, our commitment to innovation and sustainable practices is reflected in our state-of-the-art solar farm. This commitment aligns perfectly with the report's emphasis on green energy initiatives and the push by African governments to reduce carbon footprints. Notably, Kenya leads with 93% of its energy from renewable sources, setting a precedent for data centres, including ours, to adopt renewable energy sources for operational efficiency and environmental responsibility.

The report also sheds light on the challenges and growth factors in the industry. The need for improved bandwidth reliability, cost-effectiveness, and enhanced knowledge and skills are areas of concern. Onix Data Centre, with its focus on delivering reliable and efficient services, contributes to overcoming these barriers, ensuring that our clients have access to world-class data solutions.

Furthermore, the expansion of cloud services remains a focal point. With major players like Microsoft, AWS, and Google Cloud gradually increasing their presence in the region, Onix Data Centre is poised to collaborate and support these hyperscalers, offering a robust infrastructure that complements their expansion strategies.

In conclusion, as the "Africa Interconnection Report 2023" demonstrates, the Sub-Saharan Africa region is on the cusp of a data and cloud services revolution. Onix Data Centre, with its innovative approach and commitment to sustainability, is not just a part of this narrative but is leading the charge in Ghana and beyond. For more detailed insights, we encourage you to explore the full report HERE.

item.title: Navigating the Future: Reflecting on Vertiv's 2024 Data Centre Trends and Their Implications for Onix Data Centre
item.dc:creator: Samuel
item.content:encoded:
In the rapidly evolving world of data centre technology, staying ahead means keeping a keen eye on emerging trends. Onix Data Centre, in line with our commitment to innovation and excellence, is excited to delve into the recent insights provided by our partner, Vertiv. Their article on the key data centre infrastructure and energy trends for 2024 not only offers a glimpse into the future but also helps guide our ongoing strategic discussions.

Exploring the Trends

Vertiv's insights highlight several critical developments that are shaping the data centre industry:

1. The Growing Role of AI: The increasing integration of AI in digital infrastructure is leading to greater energy demands and a need for more advanced infrastructure. While we are exploring ways to accommodate these needs, we recognise the importance of developing AI-ready data centres.

2. Adapting to AI's Demands: The challenge of retrofitting traditional data centres to support AI's intensive computing requirements is clear. We acknowledge the need for modernisation and are actively considering the most effective paths forward, including potential modular and liquid cooling solutions.

3. Innovations in Energy Storage: Vertiv's emphasis on advanced energy storage systems like BESS represents an important shift towards sustainability in the industry. While we have not finalised our approach in this area, we are closely monitoring these developments to inform our future energy strategies.

4. Diverse and Scalable Infrastructure: The expansion of cloud and colocation services, along with varied enterprise data centre investments, underscores the need for flexible infrastructure. This aligns with our commitment to providing scalable solutions that can adapt to changing client needs.

5. Elevated Importance of Cloud Security: As reliance on cloud services grows, so does the need for robust security measures. We continue to prioritise the security of our data centres, ensuring the protection of our clients' data in alignment with evolving global standards.

Onix Data Centre's Perspective

At Onix Data Centre, these trends from Vertiv are more than just market observations; they help guide our strategic thinking. We understand the significance of AI in shaping the future of data centres and are in the process of evaluating how best to adapt our facilities and services to these evolving demands.

Exploring AI-Ready Possibilities: Recognising the impact of AI, we are actively exploring what it means to be AI-ready. While specific investments are still under discussion, we acknowledge the importance of evolving our infrastructure to support AI applications.

Sustainable Energy Solutions: Sustainability is at the core of our mission. We are keenly observing the advancements in energy storage solutions like BESS, considering how they could be integrated into our future energy strategy to enhance efficiency and reduce environmental impact.

Adaptable Infrastructure Solutions: In response to the diverse and expanding needs of our clients, we remain committed to offering flexible and scalable data centre solutions. Our approach is to tailor our services to meet the dynamic requirements of both cloud providers and enterprise clients.

Commitment to Security: In an era where data security is paramount, we continue to invest in state-of-the-art security measures. Our commitment is to provide a secure environment that meets the stringent compliance standards of various regions.

As the data centre landscape continues to evolve, driven by technological advancements like AI, Onix Data Centre is not just observing but actively participating in shaping the future. We are committed to staying informed and adaptable, ensuring that our services will meet the challenges and opportunities of tomorrow.

Join us on this journey into the future of data centres. Discover how Onix Data Centre is preparing for the evolving demands of the digital world. Contact us and tell us your thoughts.

item.title: Can Solar Power Revolutionise Data Centres for a Sustainable Future?
item.dc:creator: Samuel
item.content:encoded:
In the digital age, data centres are indispensable to the fabric of global connectivity, empowering cloud services, big data analytics, and a multitude of other digital services that drive modern life. Yet, as these facilities burgeon in importance, so too does the scrutiny of their environmental footprint. This raises a crucial question: Can solar power revolutionise data centres for a sustainable future? Onix Data Centres has not only pondered this question but is actively demonstrating that the answer is a resounding 'yes.'

The Essential Role of Data Centres

The digital transformation has magnified the demand for robust, secure, and efficient data centres. These facilities are pivotal for processing and storing the burgeoning amounts of data generated daily. However, the consequential energy consumption poses significant environmental challenges. Onix Data Centres has embraced these challenges, pioneering a path that intertwines operational excellence with environmental stewardship.

The Onix Solar Solution

From the outset, Onix Data Centres made a strategic choice to harness solar power. Our installation, featuring a sophisticated array of 2,200 panels, has been tailored to match our energy requirements precisely, creating an exemplar of efficiency in the data centre sector. By capping our solar plant's output at 105kW, we ensure the optimal use of our generated power, reflecting our commitment to sustainable practices and the judicious management of resources.

Cutting Costs and Carbon Footprints

The economic advantages of solar energy are as clear as the environmental ones. Operational costs are a primary concern for any data centre, and at Onix, we have significantly reduced these expenses by adopting solar power. While we've always utilised solar energy, our operational costs are markedly lower than those of typical data centres reliant on conventional power. The daily production of 1,200 kWh from our solar farm contributes not just to the sustainability of our operations but also to a pricing structure that benefits our clients.

Ensuring Reliability and Scalability

Reliability and scalability are the twin pillars of energy supply for data centres. Onix's solar infrastructure, with its peak potential of 640kW, demonstrates the capability of solar to deliver a consistent, expandable energy solution. It's a commitment that mirrors the reliability that our clients expect from us — uninterrupted service, powered by a clean, renewable source.

The Broader Impact of the Onix Approach

Onix's solar-powered operations have wider implications for the data centre industry. By leading with a model that showcases sustainability's economic and environmental benefits, Onix Data Centres is helping redefine what it means to be a responsible digital infrastructure provider in the 21st century.

The fusion of solar power and data centre operations is a movement gaining momentum, with Onix Data Centres at the forefront. Our dedication to optimising solar energy use is a testament to the practicality and necessity of renewable sources in the digital landscape. It's a journey towards a brighter future, where technology and sustainability progress in unison, powered by the sun.

If you’re inspired by the potential of a solar-powered data centre and curious about how Onix Data Centres can empower your business, we invite you to reach out. Together, we can explore a partnership that aligns with your sustainability goals and our commitment to a greener future.

For more information or to start a conversation about your data centre needs, contact us today. Discover how your data can be powered by the sun, with Onix Data Centres.

item.title: The Role of Edge Computing in Ghana's Digital Transformation in Ghana
item.dc:creator: Samuel
item.content:encoded:
As Ghana embarks on a journey towards digital transformation, a key player in this evolution is something called Edge Computing. Imagine you're using a smartphone to check the weather in your local area. Instead of sending this request over long distances to a far-off data centre, what if the information could be processed right near you, almost instantly?

That's Edge Computing in a nutshell. It's like having a mini-computer close by that can quickly process data, make decisions, and take action without needing to go on a long trip across the internet. Onix Data Centre is keeping a close eye on this technology, aiming to help spread its benefits across Ghana. This could mean faster internet services, more reliable online tools, and even new technologies that can operate more efficiently, all contributing to Ghana's growth in the digital world.

 1. Understanding Reduced Latency Nationwide

Edge Computing significantly reduces latency, enabling real-time data processing essential for applications requiring immediate analysis and action, such as AI-driven analytics and IoT deployments. This reduction in latency is crucial for enhancing operational efficiency and responsiveness, particularly in industries where speed is of the essence. Through its exploration of Edge Computing, Onix Data Centre recognises the potential for Ghanaian businesses, irrespective of their geographical locations, to benefit from improved data processing speeds.

 2. Securing Data Transactions Across Ghana

The shift towards Edge Computing offers enhanced data security by processing information closer to its source. This localised processing approach minimises the risks associated with transferring data over long distances, potentially reducing exposure to data breaches. By observing these developments, Onix Data Centre underscores the importance of robust security measures and the role of Edge Computing in creating a more secure digital ecosystem for businesses operating within Ghana.

 3. Facilitating Scalability and Flexibility for Businesses

Edge Computing provides scalable and flexible solutions that allow businesses to swiftly adapt to market changes and operational demands. This adaptability is particularly relevant for Ghana's growing digital economy, where businesses range from startups to large corporations. The exploration of Edge Computing by entities like Onix Data Centre highlights the technology's capacity to support businesses in scaling their operations efficiently and maintaining competitiveness in a fast-evolving digital environment.

 4. Promoting Cost Efficiency in Digital Operations

The adoption of Edge Computing can lead to significant cost savings for businesses by streamlining data processing and reducing bandwidth usage. This cost efficiency supports the creation of a more competitive business landscape, enabling companies to allocate resources more effectively and foster innovation. Observations from Onix Data Centre suggest that Edge Computing could be a key factor in optimising operational expenses across various sectors in Ghana.

 5. Ensuring Reliability and Uptime in Digital Services

Edge Computing enhances system reliability and uptime by distributing processing tasks, thus mitigating the impact of single points of failure. The infrastructure and technical expertise at Onix Data Centre, including its Tier IV certification, reflect a commitment to high availability and operational excellence. Such advancements in Edge Computing infrastructure could significantly contribute to maintaining continuous digital services across Ghana, supporting critical operations nationwide.

 Conclusion

The exploration and adoption of Edge Computing are critical to Ghana's digital transformation journey. As the country embraces this technology, understanding its benefits and challenges becomes paramount. Onix Data Centre, through its ongoing projects and research into Edge Computing, aims to be at the forefront of this transformation, providing insights and infrastructure that support the nation's digital economy. The collective efforts in this direction promise to usher in a new era of efficiency, security, and innovation for businesses and consumers alike.

 Moving Forward

For stakeholders interested in the digital future of Ghana, the evolution of Edge Computing offers exciting opportunities for growth and development. Engaging with these technologies, sharing knowledge, and participating in collaborative projects are essential steps towards realising the full potential of Ghana's digital transformation. If you want to hear more about Onix' thoughts on edge computing, contact us.

item.title: Ensuring Digital Resilience in West Africa: Onix Data Centres' Strategic Edge Amidst Internet Outages
item.dc:creator: Samuel
item.content:encoded:
Recent undersea cable failures have triggered a significant digital disruption across West and Central Africa, starkly highlighting the fragility of the global internet infrastructure. Countries such as Ghana have been severely impacted, with businesses coming to the realisation that their reliance on a single or limited number of Internet Service Providers (ISPs) or overseas hosting services exposes them to substantial operational risks

A Stark Realisation for Self-Hosted Servers

For businesses that have opted to host their own servers, this incident has served as a stark wake-up call. It's become clear that an event like this can disrupt an entire business, underscoring the inadequacy of traditional IT infrastructures during such crises. An IT room with servers connected to merely one or, at best, two ISPs falls short of providing the necessary resilience to withstand global internet disruptions.

Onix Data Centres: Elevating Resilience

In contrast to these vulnerabilities, Onix Data Centres offers a robust solution through its connections to over 15 network providers. This diverse network ensures businesses can maintain uninterrupted operations during global disruptions, highlighting the critical role of data centres in securing operational continuity in today's interconnected environment. With up to 15 backup links and more on the horizon, Onix affords businesses not just a future-proof but also a present-proof strategy against internet outages.

The Hazards of Overseas Hosting

The dependency on overseas hosting platforms like AWS and Microsoft has been critically examined, as the cable breakage revealed the fragility of relying on international connectivity. The strategic importance of local hosting has come to the fore, advocating for businesses' operations to be safeguarded against similar disruptions. By hosting data and servers within Ghana, Onix Data Centres ensures operational continuity, accentuating the significance of local data sovereignty for enhanced security and compliance.

Embracing Local Hosting with Onix

Onix Data Centres offers more than resilience; it provides a pathway to operational excellence amidst global digital vulnerabilities. The emphasis on data sovereignty, secure and compliant local hosting, presents a strategic advantage for businesses re-evaluating their digital infrastructure in the wake of the undersea cable failures.

A Strategic Call to Action

Following the recent internet outages, Onix Data Centres invites businesses to reconsider their digital strategies, stressing the importance of robust, resilient, and locally compliant hosting solutions. This incident acts as a potent reminder of the need for reliable digital infrastructure capable of withstanding the unforeseen, ensuring businesses in Ghana and across West and Central Africa can sustain their operations without interruption.

In an era defined by digital uncertainties, the resilience offered by Onix Data Centres exemplifies the strategic foresight necessary to navigate the challenges of our interconnected world. Businesses are encouraged to discover how local hosting with Onix can transform their approach to digital operations, securing their digital future against the unexpected.

Reach out to us at info@onixdatacentres.com with your enquiries and we will support you to stay online whatever the disruption.

item.title: Onix Data Centres Introduces Revolutionary Cloud/Virtual Computing Service in Ghana
item.dc:creator: Samuel
item.content:encoded:
Accra, Ghana – 26th of March, 2024 – In an exciting move set to transform the digital landscape of Ghana, Onix Data Centres announces the launch of its pioneering Cloud Edge Computing and Virtual Machine Platform. Aimed at businesses of all sizes, this service is designed to demystify cloud technology and make cutting-edge computing accessible to all. 

Simplifying Cloud Computing for Every Business 

Understanding that the concept of virtual machines (VMs) may be new to many, Onix Data Centres has crafted a platform that not only leverages the power of cloud computing but does so in a way that is understandable and accessible to everyone. Virtual machines are are servers in the cloud that can be customised to meet any purpose, allowing for greater efficiency, flexibility, digital security and most importantly costs. 

Key Benefits for Ghanaian Businesses: 

  • Flexibility and Scalability: Easily adjust your computing resources to match your business needs, without the need for physical hardware upgrades. 
  • Enhanced Security: Keep your data safe with advanced security features, including a virtual firewall and scheduled backups. 
  • Cost-Effective: Virtual servers do not require you to purchase any servers.  Reduce your IT expenses by paying only for the computing resources you use, eliminating the need for significant upfront investments in hardware. 
  • Disaster Recovery: Implement robust disaster recovery plans with ease, ensuring that your business remains operational even in the face of unexpected challenges. Virtual machines allow you to create a backup site in case of any major disasters. 

Powered by the latest Intel XEON scalable processors and built on ultra-high-speed Solid State Drive (SSD) storage, the platform is designed to handle a wide array of workloads, from Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Data Analytics to High-Performance Computing (HPC), with unmatched speed and efficiency. 

Our virtual machines at Onix start from 1 vCPU all the way up to 16 vCPU's. Virtual machines can be provisioning rapidly within minutes, to have access to additional infrastructure immediately allowing you to scale immediately

An Exclusive Offer to Get You Started 

To make this technology even more accessible, Onix Data Centres is delighted to offer a one-month free trial of its VM service. This no-obligation trial allows businesses to experience the benefits of cloud computing firsthand, with the option to continue on a monthly recurring charge (MRC) basis. 

About Onix Data Centres 

Onix Data Centres is at the forefront of providing innovative data centre solutions in Ghana, dedicated to empowering businesses with the tools they need to succeed in a digital world. Our commitment to accessibility, reliability, and security ensures that your business has the support it needs to grow and thrive. 

For more information on how you can leverage Onix Data Centres’ Cloud Edge Computing and Virtual Machine Platform to transform your business, please visit www.onixdatacentres.com or contact us directly by email.
